vo: Your body whispers.
Before it screams.
Here are eight warning signs you should never ignore.

scenes.title: Chest pain or pressure
scenes.detail: Tightness or squeezing that spreads to your arm, jaw or back
vo: One. Chest pain or pressure that spreads to your arm, jaw, or back.
It could be a heart attack. Call emergency services now.

scenes.title: Face drooping, arm weakness, slurred speech
scenes.detail: Remember F.A.S.T. — Face, Arms, Speech, Time
vo: Two. A drooping face. A weak arm. Slurred speech.
That's a stroke. Every minute counts. Call for help.

scenes.title: The worst headache of your life
scenes.detail: Sudden, explosive and unlike anything before
vo: Three. A sudden, severe headache. The worst of your life.
It can mean bleeding in the brain. Get emergency care.

scenes.title: Breathless doing everyday things
scenes.detail: Stairs, walking or lying flat suddenly leave you winded
vo: Four. Getting breathless doing things that used to be easy.
Your heart or lungs may be struggling. See a doctor.

scenes.title: Constant thirst & frequent urination
scenes.detail: Often with blurry vision, tiredness or slow-healing cuts
scenes.action: Ask for a blood sugar test
vo: Five. Constant thirst, and frequent urination.
Classic signs of diabetes. A simple blood test can tell you.

scenes.title: Losing weight without trying
scenes.detail: Around 5% of your body weight in 6–12 months, with no change in diet or exercise
vo: Six. Losing weight without trying.
It can point to thyroid problems, diabetes, or cancer. Get it checked.

scenes.title: A mole that changes
scenes.detail: New, growing, bleeding or changing in shape or color — or a sore that won't heal
vo: Seven. A mole that changes size, shape, or color.
Skin cancer is highly treatable, when it's caught early.

scenes.title: Blood where it shouldn't be
scenes.detail: In your stool or urine — or bowel habits that change for weeks
vo: Eight. Blood in your stool or urine.
It can be an early sign of bowel, bladder, or kidney disease. Don't let embarrassment cost you.
Listening to your body isn't fear. It's self-respect.
Caught early, most serious conditions are far more treatable.
So don't wait for the scream.
Book the check-up you've been putting off. Today.
And share this with someone you love.
